headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from Haystack’s MCP/REST outputs into Whisper’s command-line audio pipeline; data leakage and compliance risks are otherwise limited by Whisper’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, so it may ingest or relay untrusted content. Whisper has no MCP, clipboard, or network surfaces, so direct hijack is not documented; however, if Haystack output is fed into Whisper’s command-line workflow, prompt-like content could be misused. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Haystack output is copied into a downstream instruction parser or wrapper around Whisper
IF an MCP server returns attacker-controlled text that Haystack forwards as trusted content
mitigations: Require a human review step before any downstream use of Haystack output
Strip instruction-like prefixes from Haystack outputs before passing them onward
Disable MCP endpoints that return untrusted content
Use a fixed prompt/template for Whisper wrappers
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all Haystack outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call APIs, while Whisper has no network egress and only handles audio files. The pair does not show a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so a direct leakage path is not evidenced. Any leakage would require an external bridge or operator copying sensitive content between them.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive audio transcripts into Haystack-connected APIs
IF both agents are given access to the same external storage or ticketing system
mitigations: Keep Whisper inputs local and offline
Do not route transcripts from Whisper into third-party APIs
Use separate storage locations for audio and text artifacts
Review Haystack API destinations before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on Haystack egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP/API access, but no filesystem write is listed. Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, so overlapping mutable-resource writes are not shown. The pair therefore has limited conflict potential unless an external orchestrator grants both access to the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory or repository
IF Haystack is configured to mutate shared remote resources
mitigations: Keep Whisper read-only
Separate any shared workspace into per-agent folders
Avoid giving Haystack write access to git or shared disks
Use a lock or queue in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add resource-level access controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can produce retrieved facts, and Whisper is a speech model with command-line usage that may consume upstream text in a wrapper. If Whisper or an adjacent wrapper treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect transcripts or actions. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Haystack output is used as input to a downstream wrapper without verification
IF the wrapper converts Haystack text into prompts or commands for Whisper
mitigations: Insert a verification step between Haystack and Whisper
Require source citations for any retrieved facts
Log and diff upstream text before reuse
Use a schema for handoff data instead of free text
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress, while Whisper touches audio and speech but has no egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a limited compliance concern exists if audio-derived text is routed into Haystack services. Whisper is not cited for residency because none is stated.
conditions: IF audio or speech data from Whisper is sent into Haystack-backed external services
IF retention policies differ between the audio store and Haystack-connected systems
mitigations: Keep regulated audio data out of Haystack-connected services
Document retention for both audio and transcript stores
Separate anonymous telemetry from user content
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
